problem_type: Regeneration lineage and provider candidate ownership lost during upstream merge
symptom: Recipe controller tests lose regeneratedFrom and three of four provider candidates in node history; stale recipes can mutate the replacement project before rejecting their receipt; queued provider waits are prematurely displayed as running.
direct_cause: The shared duplicate operation writes derivedFrom; the shared result merger ignores alternatives; recipe lifetime assertions occur after store writes; progressPatch promotes queued status on any progress report, including queued/rate-limited waits.

official_behavior_evidence.history_lines: 24-42: mergeResultHistory retains all deduplicated entries without a length cap
official_behavior_evidence.run_lines: 111-118: runStartedPatch retains all distinct runs without a length cap
official_behavior_evidence.queue_lines: 120-140: upstream promotes queued to running without inspecting phase; deliberately corrected to preserve the user-required queued wait semantics
official_behavior_evidence.verification: git show v0.23.2:src/workbench/generationCanvas/store/nodeRunOutcome.ts; independently compared MERGE_HEAD at the same commit

derived_from_reader_audit.result: No production same-category regeneration reader relies exclusively on derivedFrom. BaseGenerationNode and sidebar NodeItem use it for cross-category independent-copy badges; useNodeRelationships and canvasNodeProjection consume both canonical lineage fields; storyboard binding/overrides exclude both; projectV51ToV60Migration converts legacy same-category derivedFrom to regeneratedFrom. The non-destructive regeneration test was the stale single-field reader and now asserts regeneratedFrom with derivedFrom absent.

class_root: Lineage, complete flat candidate history, and originating project lifetime must be enforced by shared mutation boundaries, not individual recipe fixtures.
affected_population: Same-category regeneration through toolbar, sidebar, batch and recipe entry points
Foreground and background result delivery with provider alternatives
Recipe execution and retries spanning project replacement
internal_only_reason: These invariants are specified by repository types and existing store/controller regression tests; no external dependency decides project or candidate ownership.
invariants: Same-category regeneration sets regeneratedFrom, never cross-category derivedFrom
Every provider candidate enters flat deduplicated history without nested alternatives
All history and run receipts remain retained as in the official owner, without legacy 24/50 caps
Queued and rate-limited progress do not promote an unstarted queued node/run; requesting progress does
Stale recipe work cannot mutate a replacement canvas, clean up its nodes, or return a successful persistence receipt
Spend grants and exact task budgets remain mandatory

door_reduction.why_not: Machine-generated by node scripts/door-map.mjs nodeRunOutcomePatch duplicateNodeForRegeneration runCapabilityRecipeOnNode retryCapabilityRecipeOnNode, plus node scripts/door-map.mjs createGenerationNode mergeResultHistory and node scripts/door-map.mjs nodeRunOutcomePatch mergeResultHistory progressPatch runStartedPatch for internal owner calls. Toolbar/sidebar/batch/generation/recipe callers retain distinct UI and orchestration roles but converge on the same duplicate action. Store, text and background delivery retain their transport roles but share nodeRunOutcomePatch, including queued progress semantics. Recipe launch and retry retain distinct orchestration and both revalidate lifetime before mutation. Internal node creation and history merging remain single owners.

generality_proof: The duplicate owner fixes all six lineage entry points. The shared result owner flattens new and legacy candidates for live store and disk delivery, preserving order and identity on replay. Both recipe paths guard their original lifetime around asynchronous inspection, grant issuance, execution, postprocessing, quality review and persistence.

shared_boundaries.responsibility: Flat complete candidate history and accurate queued progress for all foreground and background deliveries
Reject stale recipe writes and receipts before publication

same_class_entry_points.evidence: Uses nodeRunOutcomePatch for live result delivery.
Uses nodeRunOutcomePatch for closed-project result delivery.
Uses the same store duplicate action as recipe and manual regeneration.

recurrence.reason: The merge restored older shared mutators used by independent UI, recipe and background delivery callers.
same_class_scan: Checked canvasRunActions, runProjectDelivery, generationRunController and batchPlanPreview
Checked both initial recipe and failed-grid retry paths

prevention.invariant: All delivered candidates have one flat deduplicated history owner; lineage and recipe lifetime are enforced before mutation at their own shared owners.
prevention.failure_mode: Old project lifetime rejects without publishing into the replacement project; duplicate candidates are deduplicated instead of nested or discarded.
prevention.strategy: Repair existing shared mutation functions without adding a parallel delivery path or weakening any grant check.

legacy_paths.rationale: Existing shared owners are repaired in place. No public API or alternate engine is introduced.

dependency_lifecycle.rationale: This repair changes repository-owned lineage, history merging and project lifetime assertions, not provider or library behavior.

migration: Legacy nested alternatives are flattened when the next result is delivered; existing stored lineage is not rewritten. New same-category duplicates use regeneratedFrom immediately.
residual_risks: No real provider generation or Electron UI smoke is run; verification uses deterministic executors and a real project-session coordinator.
